trend.title: CRED iQ: CMBS Distress Hits 11.2% as Stress Shifts From New York to Los Angeles, Chicago and Houston
trend.scope: U.S. conduit and SASB CMBS loans (CRED iQ October 2026 loan data, as reported by CRE Daily)
trend.metric: 11.2% of $617 billion in conduit and SASB loans distressed (10.9% a year earlier); Chicago 23.5%, Houston 15.3%, Los Angeles 14.6%, New York 11.2%
trend.summary: CRED iQ's October loan data put 11.2% of the $617 billion in conduit and SASB loans in distress, up from 10.9% a year earlier, with the stress moving away from New York. New York improved to 11.2% from 12.5%, while Los Angeles jumped to 14.6% from 9.4%, Houston rose to 15.3% from 12.4% and Chicago to 23.5% from 19.5%. Office distress runs 16.4% nationally and represents 44% of troubled balance; office distress reached 21.5% in Los Angeles (from 9.9%), 32.6% in Chicago and 31.5% in Houston (from 21.9%). In Los Angeles, Equitable Plaza's $74 million loan came due again and wasn't repaid, with a latest valuation of $57.7 million against $150.5 million at origination, and Philadelphia's 99.5%-leased 2400 Market Street also hit a maturity wall.
trend.significance: Defaults driven by maturity and refinancing at current rates and values, rather than occupancy, tend to produce disputes over extensions, modifications and forbearance, guarantor and recourse carve-out claims, receivership and foreclosure timing, and mezzanine intercreditor conflicts. Owners and guarantors in the newly stressed metros, special servicers, and lenders weighing refinancings should expect more contested workouts, particularly where values sit far below origination.

verification.quote: Of the $617 billion in conduit and SASB loans, 11.2% is now distressed, up from 10.9% a year earlier.
New York improved, sliding to 11.2% from 12.5%. Los Angeles went the other way, jumping to 14.6% from 9.4%.
Houston rose to 15.3% from 12.4%, and Chicago to 23.5%, up from 19.5% last year.

verification.claim: Office nationally and in Los Angeles
verification.quote: Office distress runs 16.4% nationally and represents 44% of troubled balance. In Los Angeles it more than doubled, from 9.9% to 21.5%.

Equitable Plaza’s $74 million loan came due again Oct. 6 after an extension and wasn’t repaid. The tower’s latest valuation of $57.7 million sits far below the $150.5 million it carried at origination.
In Houston the office rate rose from 21.9% to 31.5%
2400 Market Street in Philadelphia is 99.5% leased
